text: Include a protein source at every meal to protect muscle while you train.
Warm up for five minutes before any session; cold muscles fatigue faster.
Progress one variable each week: reps, sets or time, never all three at once.
Sleep seven to nine hours, because recovery happens in bed, not during the workout.
Drink water before, during and after training; thirst means you are already behind.
Keep your knees tracking over your toes through every squat and lunge.
Walk 7,000 to 9,000 steps on rest days to aid recovery without adding fatigue.
Log each session so you can beat your last performance instead of guessing.
Rest 30 to 60 seconds on conditioning blocks and up to 90 seconds on strength work.
Fill half your plate with vegetables to stay satisfied on fewer calories.
Stop every set two reps before your form breaks, not after.
Stretch hips and chest daily if you sit for more than six hours.
Place your largest carbohydrate portion around your training window.
Skip the perfect plan and follow the one you can repeat for twelve weeks.
